Maria H: Heads up — after the k8s 1.28 roll in eu-west yesterday the cluster-autoscaler stopped honoring GPU nodepool selectors and started provisioning CPU-only nodes into GPU nodegroups :confused:
Aj Patel: Whoa, saw autoscaler churn alerts too. Any controller errors in the logs? :eyes:
Maria H: Logs show the autoscaler refused to scale existing gpupool and created fallback nodes. Snippet: `E1003 03:12:11 main.go:412] can't find node group matching predicate: selector parsing failed: unknown field "gpuPoolRef"`
Zack R: That msg smells like an API field rename in the cloud provider nodegroup CRD after the upgrade. We had a similar drift with nodeclass last year.
Kai L: Confirmed — the cloudprovider NodeGroup CRD was updated to v1beta2 in the distro, field `gpuPoolRef` moved under `spec.providerRef`. Autoscaler shim still reads old path.
Maria H: Yeah, autoscaler binary is the release pinned at deploy-time. It treats the selector parse error as "no matching nodegroup" so it falls back to generic provisioner -> CPU nodes. Costy.
Aj Patel: Can we hotfix by adding a compat migration in the autoscaler or patch the CRD to expose the old path? Which is lower risk?
Zack R: Patch CRD temporarily with compatibility webhook would be quickest (surgical). But operator upgrade path might reapply the new schema. Safer to roll a small autoscaler patch that accepts both shapes — grep for providerRef or gpuPoolRef.
Maria H: I'll spin a canary autoscaler image with tolerant parsing and deploy to canary cluster. Any test checklist?
Kai L: Test cases: 1) scale-up request for pod with `nvidia.com/gpu:1`; 2) labels-based selection matching gpupool; 3) taint/toleration path still respected. If canary passes, promote to prod.
InfraBot: Deploy started: canary/autoscaler:v2026-compat-parse -> eu-west-canary at 2026-10-03T06:05:00Z
sre-oncall: During canary, observed a transient spike in preemption warnings — looks like the fallback nodes were created before canary took effect. Watch node churn metrics (node_create_rate, node_delete_rate).
Maria H: Canary passed basic smoke tests. Verified `kubectl get nodes -l node.k8s.redwood/gpu-pool=mx` picks up new GPU nodes created by autoscaler. Logs show no selector parse error anymore.
Aj Patel: Nice. Let's prepare an infra PR: (1) autoscaler tolerant parser (unit tests), (2) rollout plan (canary -> staggered), (3) crd-compat note for ops. Also add alert for selector-parse-failures so we catch regression next time.
Zack R: One more thing — we should add a fallback policy flag to disable fallback CPU provisioning when GPU selectors fail. Ops could flip it during sensitive clusters.
Maria H: Good idea. I'll add CLI flag `--disable-fallback-provisioning` to the autoscaler and make default = false. Ops runbooks updated.
Kai L: After we merge, schedule a postmortem summary with timeline and cost impact estimate. I saw ~14 extra CPU nodes launched for 40m in eu-west -> ballpark $1.8k.
Maria H: Thanks everyone. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-autoscaler/pull/478 — includes parser fix + flag + tests. Planning staggered rollout this afternoon. :thumbsup:
